objective: Proof. (i) Splice lemma: if a signed piece has a parity certificate (lines covering every point evenly, with an odd number of negations) that avoids a line m, then splicing any host at an incidence of m gives a parity-unsolvable system. (ii) Two calls: with G the piece's 2x2 transfer matrix and H_k the host with one incidence replaced by a chain of k pieces, M(H) = (tr G M(H_1) - M(H_2)) / det G by Cayley-Hamilton. (iii) An eight-line piece without repeated lines has det G = -16 lam^2 (lam - 1)^6 (lam + 1)^6. So for every complex lam outside {0, 1, -1}, parity's coupling on connected simple parity-unsolvable systems is as hard as on all connected simple systems, and parity's failing class makes no member of its family easy.

title: Parity's failing systems carry every hard instance
